title: On Picking the ripest fruit first
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：pick　|　正文 349 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pick 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the operator ① picked the ripest fruit first for the whole place, and every trainee in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three shifts on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the operator ② picks the ripest fruit first without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ pick the ripest fruit first at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ picked the ripest fruit first before — a line in the log for June 1953 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Picking the ripest fruit first for the whole place, the operator said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the switch at the far screen, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ pick a whole basket of beans without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Pick a whole basket of beans at once and never mention it again.

By 1966 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the log, and a new trainee from the next station ⑧ picks a whole basket of beans for the whole place every shift without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the screen, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ picked the ripest fruit first again when nobody else would.

⑩ To pick the ripest fruit first, my mother said in 1971, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the station remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the station forgets, somebody picks the ripest fruit first without a word of thanks again and somebody must pick the ripest fruit first for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 挑选（一般过去式 picked the ripest fruit first：1959 年操作员头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 挑选（一般现在 picks the ripest fruit first：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 挑选（不定式 to pick the ripest fruit first：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 挑选（过去完成时 had picked the ripest fruit first：1953 年六月的运行日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 挑选（动名词 picking the ripest fruit first 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 采摘（pick a whole basket of beans：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去采摘满满一篮豆子）
G. v. 采摘（pick a whole basket of beans：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 挑选（后段两处：新来的实习生照例 picks a whole basket of beans，而母亲又一次 picked the ripest fruit first）

answers.why: pick 意为“挑选”，1959 年操作员替所有人挑选先挑最熟的那些果子，那是机房里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 picked。
pick 意为“挑选”，自那以后操作员不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 picks。
pick 意为“挑选”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯挑选先挑最熟的那些果子”，此处为不定式 to pick the ripest fruit first。
pick 意为“挑选”，运行日志里 六月 那行字说明早在 1966 年之前就有人挑选过，故用过去完成时 had picked。
pick 意为“挑选”，操作员说“挑选先挑最熟的那些果子这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 picking the ripest fruit first 作主语。
pick 意为“采摘”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去采摘满满一篮豆子”，should ever 之后用原形 pick a whole basket of beans。
pick 意为“采摘”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻采摘满满一篮豆子（pick a whole basket of beans at once），以后再也不要提起。
pick 意为“挑选”，新来的实习生每个班次都照例采摘满满一篮豆子，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 picks。
pick 意为“挑选”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人挑选先挑最熟的那些果子，用一般过去式 picked 叙述。
pick 意为“挑选”，结尾那句是母亲 1971 年的话：要挑选先挑最熟的那些果子，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和机房记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 pick 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1959 the operator picked the ripest fruit first for the whole place, and nobody in the station forgot it.
Even now the operator picks the ripest fruit first without a word of thanks whenever the station asks.
Picking the ripest fruit first for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever pick a whole basket of beans without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new trainee from the next station picks a whole basket of beans for the whole place every shift, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother picked the ripest fruit first again, and the station remembered that half.
